clue.text: Old entertainer, firm attraction, returning after Christmas

indicators.note: the firm and attraction come after the word for Christmas

parts.note: Noel is another name for Christmas
CO is short for company

indicators.note: the word for attraction is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a draw is something that pulls in crowds

explanation.surface: A veteran performer, a company's big crowd-puller, comes back on stage once the Christmas season is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was the English playwright, actor and songwriter of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward was a celebrated performer, songwriter and wit from a past era, so he is fairly called an old entertainer.

clue.text: Curious how patsy becomes a soft touch

indicators.note: the answer is what the word patsy turns into once its soft touch is swapped for a refusal

parts.note: taken as written
a pat is a gentle tap of the hand

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer wonders how a gullible dupe ends up being an easy mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as NO SY; put PAT where the NO is and it becomes PATSY. 'Soft touch' looks like a synonym for patsy, but it is the pat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nosy is inquisitive about other people's business, which is one sense of curious.

clue.text: Made it possible to lift key curse

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting sends the letters upward, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a keyboard
a bane is a curse or blight

explanation.surface: Someone managed to raise a key-related jinx.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable something is to allow or empower it, so made it possible is a plain synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Arrive almost full of emotion, and sort of leave

indicators.note: the word for arrive is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to come is to arrive
passionate means full of strong feeling

explanation.surface: Someone turns up nearly overwhelmed with feeling and more or less goes away again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a verb for departing; it is the noun, time off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassionate leave is time off work granted after a bereavement or family crisis, one kind of leave.

clue.text: Valuable question about fragment

indicators.note: the question word goes around the fragment, enclosing it

parts.note: why is a question word
an ort is a scrap or leftover morsel of food

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a small piece is of any worth.
explanation.walkthrough: ORT is an old word for a scrap of food, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthy means having merit or deserving esteem, close in sense to valuable.

clue.text: Intensify colour, nothing blue strangely

parts.note: red is a colour
O looks like zero

indicators.note: the word blue is set out in an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to deepen a hue, with nothing blue about it, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: To redouble efforts is to increase them greatly, so it means to intensify.

clue.text: No heart for precipitous measure

indicators.note: the word for precipitous loses one of its central letters

parts.note: steep means precipitous

explanation.surface: Someone lacks the courage for a drastic course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' looks like a measurement; it is a step in the sense of an action taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is an action taken to achieve something, as in taking measures or steps.

clue.text: Easily beat teenager, no guts and light weight

indicators.note: the teenager is disembowelled, keeping only the first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A gutless, slight youngster is easily defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to defeat them heavily and with ease.

clue.text: Perhaps fine tree one spotted in the field

parts.note: a fine is one example of a penalty
box is a tree or shrub used for hedging

explanation.surface: A fine for felling a tree seems to be imposed on someone seen out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: On a football pitch the penalty spot sits inside the penalty box, so the box is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: The penalty box is the marked area in front of goal on a football pitch, and it contains the penalty spot.

clue.text: One severely criticising prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who slams, or attacks harshly, in a review
second meaning: slang for a jail

explanation.walkthrough: Slammer is informal for jail, and a reviewer who slams something is a slammer too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a person who pans or attacks harshly and a slang term for a jail.

clue.text: Having stopped working, have ease

parts.note: a machine that died stopped working
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A broken-down worker is told to take things easy.
explanation.definitionFit: When wind or noise eases, it lessens and subsides, which is to die down.

clue.text: Local list of those to be saved in speech on revolution

parts.note: in theology, the elect are those chosen by God for salvation
oral means spoken
a roll is a turning over, a revolution

explanation.surface: A parish register of the souls to be saved, read out loud as the wheel turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The electoral roll is the register of voters in an area, so a list of local residents.

clue.text: Facing group of pupils, old master holding large book

indicators.note: the schoolmaster stands in front of the pupils, so his piece comes first
the schoolmaster word wraps around the letter for large

parts.note: beak is old slang for a schoolmaster
a house is a division of pupils in a British school

explanation.surface: An aged schoolmaster stands before a class clutching a hefty volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' looks like a painter; beak is old British slang for a teacher. British schools split pupils into houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens, and a novel is a book.

clue.text: No score, even from Anfield

indicators.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word are taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A goalless draw at Liverpool's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Anfield is the home ground of Liverpool Football Club; 'even' looks like a level score but picks the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is zero in a football result, a blank scoreline.

clue.text: Cane applied to part of body: up and down it goes

parts.note: a switch is a thin flexible rod for beating
the back is part of the body

explanation.surface: A beating with the rod across someone's back, raised and lowered repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: A switchback is also a roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a road or railway, or a fairground ride, that rises and falls steeply.

clue.text: Wife that is fatter than anyone?

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A rude question whether one's spouse is the stoutest person around.
explanation.definitionFit: Widest means broadest of all, which a fatter person than anyone else would be; the question mark flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Undue praise of cook, drinking coffee

indicators.note: the cooking word takes in the coffee, swallowing it

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A chef is complimented too much while sipping a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive or insincere compliment, which is undue praise.

clue.text: Keen to play with toys — everything depends on it

indicators.note: the letters are played around with until they form a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eager child wants to play with the toys, as if the whole world rests on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central stone of an arch that holds the rest in place, hence the thing all else depends on.

clue.text: What business makes: a small pie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the total sales a company makes
second meaning: a pastry folded over a filling

explanation.walkthrough: Turnover is both a firm's revenue and a folded pastry such as an apple turnover.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a company's sales volume and a half-moon pastry with a sweet or savoury filling.

clue.text: Series of races run say over a dry area

indicators.note: in a down clue these letters sit above the rest

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
e.g. means for example, as say does
taken as written
TT is teetotal, not drinking

explanation.surface: Racing, as it were, across a waterless stretch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting event made up of a programme of boat races.

clue.text: Quickly throwing spider, say, into river

indicators.note: the cue support goes inside the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a spider is a type of rest, the cue support used in snooker and billiards

explanation.surface: Someone hastily flings an arachnid into a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spider' looks like the creature; in snooker it is a raised rest for the cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction meaning very fast, so quickly.

clue.text: Put on the ground, drop off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to place something down
second meaning: to let a passenger out of a vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are phrasal verbs: you set down a box, and a taxi sets down a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both placing an object down and letting a passenger out of a vehicle.

clue.text: Second to be arrested by base tyrant

indicators.note: the second is held inside the base, as if taken into custody

parts.note: a depot is a military base or storehouse

explanation.surface: A deputy is detained at a military base on the orders of a dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, a tyrant.

clue.text: Stay close to tailless mammoth

indicators.note: the adjective loses its last letter

parts.note: huge means mammoth-sized

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep near a woolly mammoth that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mammoth' looks like the animal; it is the adjective meaning enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: To hug a coast or kerb is to keep close beside it.

clue.text: A leaderless gathering of troops heading off sudden attack a success for France

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the assembly loses its first letter

parts.note: a muster is an assembly of soldiers

indicators.note: the attack loses its first letter

parts.note: a blitz is a sudden intense attack

explanation.surface: A rudderless assembly of soldiers fends off a surprise assault and France wins the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Austerlitz was Napoleon's great victory of 1805 over Russia and Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Austerlitz was a decisive French military victory under Napoleon.

clue.text: Programs announced in recess

indicators.note: the word for programs is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: apps are computer programs

explanation.surface: Software releases are revealed during a parliamentary break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a holiday; it is an alcove, the apse of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Red coat tailored, 1930s style

indicators.note: the letters are cut and stitched into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A made-to-measure scarlet jacket in the fashion of the thirties.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative design movement that flourished in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Inside deck very warm, so celebrity wants to make it snappy?

definitions.text: celebrity wants to make it snappy?

indicators.note: the word for very warm goes within the deck

parts.note: the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern
hot means very warm

explanation.surface: Below deck it is sweltering, so a star asks for things to be done quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snappy' looks like brisk; here it means taking snaps, photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo op is an occasion staged for a public figure to be photographed, the snaps a celebrity seeks.

clue.text: Floor with a new riddle

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, a KO
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is stumped by a fresh puzzle and a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A koan is a paradoxical Zen Buddhist puzzle used in meditation, a kind of riddle.

clue.text: Extremely pitiable hush, in which thousands at first — die of this?

indicators.note: only the extremes of the word, its first and last letters, are kept

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the silence holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: silence is a hush

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pitiful silence falls in which thousands are the first to perish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: what many people might die of.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease such as plague, a cause of mass death.
